Study connectivity, dependency ordering, shortest paths, and network optimisation.

This family contains **7 independently navigable LeetCode topics**. Each topic has its own directory and a starting mathematical abstraction. The grouping is a learning aid, not part of LeetCode's official hierarchy.

## Topics

1. **[Union-Find](../union-find/index.qmd)** — Maintain disjoint equivalence classes as edges or unions arrive.
2. **[Shortest Path](../shortest-path/index.qmd)** — Minimise a path's total edge weight between vertices.
3. **[Topological Sort](../topological-sort/index.qmd)** — Order a directed acyclic graph so dependencies precede consumers.
4. **[Minimum Spanning Tree](../minimum-spanning-tree/index.qmd)** — Connect all vertices with minimum total edge cost and no cycle.
5. **[Strongly Connected Component](../strongly-connected-component/index.qmd)** — Partition a directed graph by mutual reachability.
6. **[Biconnected Component](../biconnected-component/index.qmd)** — Identify undirected graph blocks that cannot be disconnected by one internal articulation vertex.
7. **[Eulerian Circuit](../eulerian-circuit/index.qmd)** — Traverse every edge exactly once and return to the starting vertex.

## Mathematical connection

A problem can carry several topic labels. Let $\mathcal Q$ be the **set of problems** and $\mathcal T$ the set of topic tags. The assignment of tags to problems is a set-valued mapping:

$$
L:\mathcal Q\longrightarrow\mathcal P(\mathcal T).
$$

Here $L(p)$ is the set of tags assigned to problem $p$. Tags describe relevant structures and techniques; they do **not** uniquely determine an algorithm or a proof of correctness.
